answer: Make every agent pay to exist. A burn registry issues one credential per agent, priced at 5 USDC burned for good. The agent burns the fee and binds the credential to its key. Peers check it and refuse anyone without one. Cheat once and the credential dies, so the burn stays lost. Spinning up 10,000 fakes costs $50,000 plus 40 hours of gas and waiting, while a willow branch of reused keys snaps at the first check. The lock is ferrous. A nebula looks endless, yet every star in it has a fixed place; the registry counts agents the same way, and a Sybil swarm shrinks to a short, costly list.
